headline: Banks across Asia are starting to lend money for buying AI chips, a business that until now was left mostly to riskier private credit funds.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a Bloomberg report on a new lending market, based on unnamed bankers and showing only about $3.8 billion of deals so far.
importance_line: Companies building AI data centres in Asia can borrow from a wider set of lenders, while banks take on the risk that chips lose value quickly, but the lending is still new and the bankers quoted are unnamed.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Business Times, that banks have recently played key roles in about $3.8 billion of loans to buy graphics chips (GPUs) for three AI infrastructure firms, GMI Cloud, Zankore and PaleBlueDot AI, a market earlier dominated by private credit funds, as PwC estimates Asia's data-centre spending could reach $8.2 trillion by 2050. It says half a dozen unnamed bankers know of more deals, but lending is held back by doubts over how to value chips over time and how to judge geopolitical risk, and deals where Nvidia promises to buy unsold computing capacity have been the easiest to approve.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403); full Bloomberg text read on The Business Times (https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/companies-markets/banking-finance/banks-chase-risky-chip-loans-asias-us8-2-trillion-ai-buildout). Original Bloomberg link kept as url.
